name: AL-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+33 district is among the most Republican in the nation
Aderholt holds about $750,000 on hand; challenger has $396
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at essentially zero
No public polling; the race draws little attention or spending
model.rationale: The district's R+33 lean, Aderholt's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial advantage over a challenger with under $500 on hand leave Democrats virtually no path; markets price a Democratic win at zero.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or a sudden wave of outside spending for the Democrat would put this safely Republican race in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 4th District is one of the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+33. Longtime incumbent Robert Aderholt is seeking another term and enters the general election with a large financial edge: he has raised more than $1 million and holds about $750,000 on hand, while Democrat Amanda Pusczek has raised roughly $16,000 and reports under $500 in cash. No public polls survey the race, and prediction markets put the chance of a Democratic win near zero.

The challenger's minimal fundraising and the district's deep red tilt leave little room for competition. Barring an extraordinary development, Aderholt is positioned to win comfortably. The main uncertainty is the size of the margin rather than the outcome, since the race has drawn little attention or outside spending.
